Evidence discipline: ladder, CV, gate, backtest, lineage fingerprints

Predict -> log -> score -> drift -> retrain -> re-gate
Forecast -> P95 + headroom -> safety floor -> price -> replay to verify

nodes.rationale: The drift monitor expects one prediction per sample, but the backtest logs one per horizon-length DECISION, which is far too sparse to reach drift.min_samples. Backfill reconstructs what the prediction log would have looked like had the champion been serving all along. Only rows inside a segment are predicted.

nodes.label: Promotion Gate
nodes.rationale: A challenger is promoted only if it beats the strongest baseline on the same test window, survives rolling-origin CV (min_cv_folds_won), keeps fold-to-fold spread within max_cv_std_ratio of the baseline, and improves on the incumbent by min_improvement_pct. Rejecting is the gate working, not failing: a model worse than a trivial rule must not serve traffic, and churning the champion on noise is worse than leaving it alone.

nodes.label: Same-window champion re-scoring
nodes.rationale: Comparing a challenger against a champion's STORED MAE compares across datasets: a model scoring 4.998 was rejected against a champion measured 4.726 on an older, easier window. Incumbents are now re-scored on this run's test window (champion_mae_same_window), with the stored figure as a flagged fallback.

nodes.label: Lineage chain (prediction -> model -> features -> data -> config)
nodes.rationale: Three weeks after a demo the question is never 'what is the MAE' but 'why did the system decide that'. Recording identifiers at each stage makes the exact inputs, the config in force, and the quality warnings that applied at training time recoverable.
nodes.norm_label: lineage chain (prediction -> model -> features -> data -> config)

nodes.label: predictions table (prediction log)
nodes.rationale: Without a logged prediction/actual/abs_error table, 'the model is getting worse' is a feeling rather than a measurement.

nodes.label: Feature-version enforcement at serving
nodes.rationale: If the online store holds a different feature version than the champion was trained on, serving REFUSES rather than predicting from mismatched inputs. Training-serving skew is otherwise invisible: the numbers still look plausible.

nodes.label: Serving a baseline is a legitimate production state
nodes.rationale: The gate rejected every gradient booster, so persistence is champion for all three resources. Trained estimators and baselines are served through one interface because the consumer only asks 'what will this resource be next'; which predictor answers is a registry implementation detail.
nodes.norm_label: serving a baseline is a legitimate production state

nodes.label: Two independent drift signals
nodes.rationale: Performance drift is what matters but needs labels, arriving a horizon late and never at all if the collector stops. Feature drift (PSI) is label-free and immediate but a shifted input distribution does not always hurt accuracy. Performance drift decides; feature drift is the early warning.

nodes.label: Walk-forward replay
nodes.rationale: A snapshot answers 'what would we allocate now' but not 'what would this policy have cost over an hour and how often would it have failed'. Only replay can, and replay is the difference between a projected saving and a measured one. At each step the policy sees ONLY prior rows, then is charged for the following horizon.

nodes.label: Snapshot vs replay disclosure
nodes.rationale: A single recommendation is one instant; the backtest replays the same policy across the series. On this data the two disagree and the replay is the number to trust, so print_report and the dashboard Overview state both rather than hiding the difference.

nodes.label: Incremental ETL via stream watermark
nodes.rationale: A collector appends forever, so reprocessing the whole table each cycle gets slower without bound. StreamSource reads from a watermark and sees only new arrivals; the full-history path stays available for training.

nodes.label: Streamlit dashboard (5 tabs)
nodes.rationale: Every panel reads a stored artifact of a pipeline run rather than recomputing, so no two panels can disagree. The config editor is the deliberate exception: it writes, because changing headroom and watching the cost move is the clearest demonstration that nothing is hardcoded.

nodes.label: Baseline ladder panel
nodes.rationale: Surfaces the persistence vs persistence_lag1 gap explicitly, because an earlier version of the project measured against the second and reported the difference as model accuracy.

nodes.label: main.py menu entry point
nodes.rationale: Every option maps to a module that also runs standalone with python -m; the menu exists so the system can be driven without remembering twelve commands.

hyperedges.label: Config read/write path: reader, cache, CRUD, SQL, seed
Collection loop: load generator drives CPU, logger samples, CRUD persists to metrics
Evidence discipline: ladder, CV, gate, backtest, lineage fingerprints
Gap-awareness: detect, segment, and prove the contamination
End-to-end lineage: data fingerprint -> feature version -> model registry
Train -> log -> gate -> promote or fall back to baseline
Predict -> log -> score -> drift -> retrain -> re-gate
Forecast -> P95 + headroom -> safety floor -> price -> replay to verify
